newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WORLD CUP WIN FOR GERMANY BUT ITALY AND DUTCH SLIP UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WORLD CUP WIN FOR GERMANY BUT ITALY AND DUTCH SLIP UP.

text.p: Germany survived a scare, Italy were held to a draw and the Netherlands crashed to defeat as Europe's traditionally strongest teams had a mixed night of fortunes in their World Cup qualifiers on Wednesday.

Reigning European champions Germany came from behind to defeat Albania 3-2 in a dramatic group nine qualifier in neutral Spain, while Italy lost their 100 per cent record in group two after being held to a 0-0 draw by Poland in Chorzow.

The biggest upset came in Bursa where Turkey revived their slim hopes of qualifying from group seven with a surprise 1-0 win over the previously unblemished Dutch. The only goal came from Hakan Sukur early in the second half, but Clarence Seedorf missed a late penalty for the visitors.

Wednesday's 12 matches -- together with 11 matches played in the last four days -- completed a hectic burst of activity in the European qualifying programme and left Scotland, Ukraine and Romania buoyed with optimism after chalking up two successive wins apiece.

Scotland pulled seven points clear at the top of group four when they followed up Saturday's 2-0 win over Estonia with a 2-0 win over Austria; Ukraine followed Saturday's win over Albania to pull three points clear of Portugal at the top of group nine with a 2-1 win over Northern Ireland, while Romania followed up Saturday's 8-0 win over Liechtenstein with a 1-0 win over Lithuania.

The Romanians have the best record in Europe with five wins out of five and a goal tally of 19-0 and lead group eight by five points from Macedonia who beat the Republic of Ireland 3-2 in a match in which both teams had a man sent off.

The outstanding personal achievements on the night were by Ulf Kirsten who scored a hat-trick for Germany in 20 minutes against Albania, Primoz Gliha who scored three in 21 minutes as Slovenia battled back to draw 3-3 in Croatia, and Kevin Gallacher, who scored twice -- his first international goals for three years -- to give Scotland their win over Austria.
Kirsten, who came on as a second half substitute, pulled Germany level against Albania in the 64th minute after the Albanians took the lead through Bledar Kola with a 61st minute penalty.
Kirsten then scored in the 80th and 84th minutes before Kola scored another penalty in the last minute. Albania also missed a penalty earlier in the game.
The game was played in Spain because of the conflict in Albania.

Although Germany stay third in group nine behind new group leaders Ukraine and second-placed Portugal, they have played two matches fewer than Portugal and one fewer than Ukraine. Both have to visit Germany.

Greece also maintained their hopes of a place in the next year's finals with a 1-0 win over Bosnia in Sarajevo, the first competitive match played there since the end of the four-year-long war in the former Yugoslavia.
Yugoslavia themselves continued to re-establish themselves as a soccer power with a 2-1 win in the Czech Republic thanks to a last-minute winner from substitute Savo Milosevic.

The win took Yugoslavia to within a point of Spain at the top of group six leaving the Czech Republic, runners-up to the Germans in Euro 96 last June, floundering in fourth place and with little realistic hope of making the finals.

In other matches, Bulgaria moved into second place behind Israel in group five with a 4-1 win over Cyprus in Sofia, while Finland collected their first points of the qualifying campaign with a 2-1 group three win over Azerbaijan in Baku.
